## Fix trie setup wrongly rendering Claude Code (mcp__trie__) tool names in an… — 2026-08-01 (parent b7c2a2c0ae4f)

**Fix trie setup wrongly using MCP-prefixed tool names in opencode docs and silently wiring globally-detected agents by adding override-preference logic and an interactive disambiguation prompt.**

The root cause was two related bugs: `docs_install.install` blindly used `targets[0]` for the docs body, so registry-ordered auto-detection could put a Claude Code harness first and bake `mcp__trie__`-prefixed names into TRIE.md and AGENTS.md even in an opencode project; and `setup_cmd` silently wired every detected agent with no chance for the user to opt out.

Three production symbols address this:

- `_select_primary_target` (new, `trie/docs_install`) picks the docs body harness by preferring any bare-name override target (e.g. opencode) over non-override harnesses, regardless of detection order. All remaining targets fall into the footer.
- `detected_target_slugs` (new, `trie/mcp_install`) is the single source of truth for auto-detection, returning registry-ordered slugs of every harness whose `MCPTarget.detect()` is true.
- `_prompt_select_targets` (new, `trie/cli`) and updated `setup_cmd` together show a numbered picker when multiple agents are detected in an interactive session; non-interactive runs (CI/scripts) fall back to wiring all detected agents unchanged.

Test coverage added: `test_install_prefers_override_target_for_body_regardless_of_order`, `test_detected_target_slugs_empty_on_clean_environment`, `test_detected_target_slugs_reports_installed_in_registry_order`, `test_cli_setup_prompts_when_multiple_agents_detected`, `test_cli_setup_non_interactive_does_not_prompt`, and `test_prompt_select_targets_parses_numbers_slugs_and_all`. The existing `test_install_multiple_targets_renders_primary_in_body_and_footer_for_rest` was corrected to assert the fixed precedence.
